course_title: Special Studies in Food Science & Technology
course_description:
This course provides students the opportunity to explore interesting and relevant areas of food science and technology independently and in depth.

This course provides students the opportunity to explore interesting and relevant areas of food science and technology independently and in depth.

At the School of Agriculture and Food Sustainability, we are committed to creating an inclusive and empowering learning environment for all students. We value and respect the diverse range of experiences our students bring to their education, and we believe that this diversity is crucial for fostering a rich culture of knowledge-sharing and meaningful exploration. We hold students and staff accountable for actively contributing to establishing a respectful and supportive learning environment.

Bullying, harassment, and discrimination in any form are strictly against our principles and againstﾠ UQ Policy, ﾠand will not be tolerated. If you have any concerns about your experience in this course, we encourage you to tell a member of the course teaching team. Your well-being and a positive learning atmosphere are of utmost importance to us.

for advice.
If you have any questions about missing class activities, please contact your course coordinator.
course_aims: To provide students the opportunity to examine specific topics in food science and technology not covered in other courses in depth.

learning_outcomes.description: Develop independent research skills to compile in-depth information on novel food science/technology topics.
Apply analytical thinking to evaluate recent developments in food science/technology and report on associated challenges.
Enhance communication and presentation skills by delivering oral presentations on advanced food science/technology subjects.

assessment_details.title: Oral Presentation
assessment_details.due_date: 9/10/2026 2:00 pm Scheduling details to be confirmed via blackboard.
assessment_details.other_conditions: Peer assessed. See the conditions definitions
assessment_details.task_description: The presentation is a group work, each group consisting of 4 self-selected students, facilitated through the course Blackboard site. Students will be provided information on self-selecting groups on Blackboard. By Friday of Week 4 (my suggestion, students who have not found a group must contact the Course Coordinator for assistance. Group Investigation: Each group will explore one “Special Topic in Food” from the list provided by the course coordinator. During the allocated teaching weeks (as advised on Blackboard), groups will collaborate to discuss the topic, gather information from credible sources (e.g., lecture material, readings, library databases, books, research papers, reputable government/industry sites), and prepare a 12-minute PowerPoint presentation that must be recorded via Echo . The steps to create a Echo Video are in this link https://elearning.uq.edu.au/student-guides-ultra/echovideo-ultra-student . Students will have to come together at times convenient for the group members to assemble the presentation and to complete the task. Group members are encouraged to communicate outside regular hours to coordinate and complete the assessment. Additionally, the instructor will be available during tutorial sessions to address any queries. Recorded presentation requirements: The group must present their slides in Echo and record the presentation (slides and audio must be clearly captured). Each group must identify four key aspects of the topic and each student will take responsibility for one aspect (research + slides + presenting). The presentation should introduce the topic clearly without becoming overly technical, and then move into slightly more specific content later (e.g., referring to research and presenting at least one graph/figure/table, explained in your own words). The recorded presentation must include a short conclusion with 2–3 take-home messages and a slide at the end with the reference list. Any figures/tables used must include a source on the slide where they appear. Submission: The Echo recording file must be submitted before the due date/time through an Assignment submission link in Blackboard. Only one group member needs to submit the file, but the submission must include the topic title and the names of all group members. Peer Assessment: Each student is responsible for evaluating the individual contributions of the other three group members using the Peer Assessment form provided on Blackboard. Peer assessment contributes to an individual mark out of 10. Failure to submit the peer assessment form by the due date/time will result in 0/10 for the peer assessment component (individual mark). Marks: Presentation = 30 marks (group mark); Peer assessment = 10 marks (individual mark). Acknowledging and/or referencing AI use Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Machine Translation (MT) are emerging tools that may support students in completing this assessment task. Students may appropriately use AI and/or MT in completing this assessment task. Students must clearly reference and/or acknowledge any use of AI or MT in each instance. A failure to reference and/or acknowledge generative AI or MT use may constitute student misconduct under the Student Code of Conduct. The use of AI or MT must be referenced and/or acknowledged appropriately. Please see assessment guidelines in blackboard course site for specific instructions. Students may also refer to Library guides found under Additional assessment information > Acknowledging and referencing AI use. Read full task description Hide full task description
assessment_details.assessment_security: Open assessment: In this assessment you can use resources such as your notes, course materials, and other tools, including AI, while completing the task. The focus is not on memorising information, but on understanding, applying judgement, and demonstrating your own thinking.
assessment_details.submission_guidelines:
The task (pre-recorded video) is submitted on Blackboard, via the relevant EchoVideo link by the submission deadline. You should also retain an electronic copy of every piece of assessment you submit. Guidance for submitting an EchoVideo is on our website.
Immediately after uploading the group submission, the team member responsible for submitting the file must provide a copy of the submission receipt to all group members. This confirmation should be sent as soon as the submission is successfully uploaded to ensure that all group members have evidence that the assessment has been submitted and can verify the submission details.
Legal Declaration:
By submitting your work via this website, you formally declare that (1) it is your own original work, and no part of the work has been copied from any other source or person except where due acknowledgement is made; (2) no part of the work has been previously submitted for assessment in this or any other institution; and (3) you have read the Student Integrity and Misconduct Policy and understand its implications.
Deferral or extension
You may be able to apply for an extension .
The maximum extension allowed is 28 days. Extensions are given in multiples of 24 hours.
Since this is a group assessment, any extension request must be submitted by the group (not by individual members). The group must provide supporting information and, if requested, discuss the request with the course coordinator.
Submission of an Extension of Assessment Due Date (EADD) should be completed online through your My Requests tab via my.UQ Dashboard , in accordance with the University's Assessment Procedure (located in the Policies and Procedures section of this course profile) which outlines the requirements for requesting extensions to assessment due dates. Extensions require the correct evidence/documentation to support the requested length of time of the extension.
Late submission
A penalty of 10% of the maximum possible mark will be deducted per 24 hours from time submission is due for up to 7 days. After 7 days, you will receive a mark of 0.
For example, a report worth a maximum of 40 marks, submitted 28 hours late will incur a penalty of 8 marks. This is calculated as 2 (24 hour periods) x 10% per period x 40 marks, resulting in 8 marks deducted from the student’s mark for the assessment.
Assessment deadlines are firm and must be met. Late submission without permission or non-submission of assessable work will result in penalties being applied . Late submission of assessment will only be granted for documented medical reasons, accident, bereavement, jury service and other circumstances allowed in the UQ Policies and Procedures Library (PPL).
